record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Are the connectedness equivalence relations of graphs of uniform subexponential growth hyperfinite, where uniform subexponential growth means growth bounded by exp(r^c) for some 0 < c < 1?

evidence.quote: Problem 41. How about graphs of uniform subexponential growth, i.e., of growth less than exp(r^c) for some 0 < c < 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a Borel graph on a standard Borel space $V$, i.e. a graph whose edge set $E\subseteq V\times V$ is Borel and symmetric. Assume $G$ is locally finite (equivalently, has bounded or countable degree as needed). For $v\in V$ and $r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $B_G(v,r)$ denote the set of vertices at graph-distance at most $r$ from $v$. Say that $G$ has uniform subexponential growth if there exists a constant $0<c<1$ and a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $f(r)\le \exp(r^{c})$ for all sufficiently large $r$ such that $|B_G(v,r)|\le f(r)$ for every $v\in V$ and every $r\in\mathbb{N}$.

The connectedness equivalence relation $E_G$ on $V$ is defined by $x\,E_G\,y$ iff $x$ and $y$ lie in the same connected component of $G$. A countable Borel equivalence relation $E$ on a standard Borel space $V$ is called hyperfinite if there exists an increasing sequence $F_0\subseteq F_1\subseteq\cdots$ of Borel equivalence relations on $V$ with finite classes such that $E=\bigcup_n F_n$.

Question: Is the connectedness equivalence relation $E_G$ of every Borel graph $G$ of uniform subexponential growth (in the sense above) hyperfinite?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work establishes that Borel graphs of polynomial growth have hyperfinite connectedness equivalence relations (Bernshteyn–Yu and related work on Borel asymptotic dimension), and that Borel graphs of subexponential growth are measure-hyperfinite. However, whether the connectedness equivalence relation of every Borel graph of uniform subexponential growth (growth bounded by $\exp(r^c)$ for some $0<c<1$) is hyperfinite in the Borel sense remains an open problem as of recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Borel Vizing's Theorem for Graphs of Subexponential Growth
status_evidence.snippet: Borel graphs of subexponential growth are measure hyperfinite; Borel hyperfiniteness in this regime is open.
status_evidence.claim: Hyperfiniteness for Borel graphs of subexponential growth (in the Borel, not just measurable, sense) is not established.

status_evidence.title: Large-scale geometry of Borel graphs of polynomial growth
status_evidence.snippet: Borel graphs of polynomial growth are hyperfinite via finite Borel asymptotic dimension.
status_evidence.claim: The polynomial-growth case is solved, leaving the subexponential-growth case as the next natural open question.

status_evidence.title: Borel asymptotic dimension and hyperfinite equivalence relations
status_evidence.snippet: Develops Borel asymptotic dimension techniques used in the polynomial-growth hyperfiniteness results.
status_evidence.claim: Current techniques cover polynomial growth but not uniform subexponential growth.
